title: AlphaAgent: LLM-Driven Alpha Mining with Regularized Exploration to Counteract Alpha Decay

problem.claim: Alpha mining must discover predictive signals while addressing alpha decay, in which factors lose predictive power over time.

gap.claim: Genetic programming is susceptible to overfitting and rapid alpha decay, while LLM-driven approaches often lack regularization against factor homogenization, producing crowded signals and accelerated decay.

contributions.claim: AlphaAgent is an autonomous framework integrating LLM-driven agents with ad hoc regularization to mine decay-resistant alpha factors.
The framework uses AST-based originality enforcement, LLM-evaluated hypothesis-factor alignment, and AST-based complexity control.
The mechanisms guide alpha generation toward originality, financial rationale, and adaptability to evolving market conditions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive evaluations reportedly show that AlphaAgent outperforms traditional and LLM-based methods in mitigating alpha decay across bull and bear markets.
The reported evaluations cover Chinese CSI 500 and U.S. S&P 500 markets over the past four years and describe consistently significant alpha.
The authors report notable resistance to alpha decay and potential for yielding powerful factors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Alpha mining seeks predictive signals for future asset returns in complex financial markets.
Alpha decay undermines factor predictive power over time, with overfitting and factor homogenization contributing to the problem.
AlphaAgent addresses the challenge through LLM-driven agents combined with regularization based on AST similarity, semantic alignment, and structural complexity constraints.
These mechanisms aim to balance originality, financial rationale, and adaptability to mitigate alpha decay.
The authors report superior decay mitigation and significant alpha across bull and bear markets in Chinese CSI 500 and U.S. S&P 500 markets.

source_observation.claim: The framework applies separate controls for originality, semantic alignment, and structural complexity during alpha generation.

interpretation.claim: Combining diversity, rationale, and complexity constraints may help reduce overfitting and homogenization in generated signals.

application.claim: A signal-generation system could use structural similarity checks, semantic consistency evaluations, and complexity limits as complementary regularizers.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which mechanism is necessary or sufficient, or whether the same controls transfer beyond the reported markets and period.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation baselines, datasets beyond the named markets, or exact performance metrics.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablation results, statistical uncertainty, or evidence independent of the authors' reported evaluations.
